summary.text: A 52-year-old man was diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme after several weeks of cognitive decline, headaches, gait ataxia and a series of epileptic seizures. Radiotherapy up to 60 Gy with simultaneous temozolomide began 53 days after surgery, delayed by complicated wound healing. His general state was unfavorable, with a Karnofsky score of 50 and right-side hemiparesis, so adjuvant temozolomide was ruled out and rehabilitation started.

Rehabilitation was discontinued 128 days after surgery because of another series of seizures, and antiepileptic treatment and steroids were escalated. CT and Fet-PET showed progressive intracranial tumor burden considered non-suitable for tumor-specific treatment. An alternative practitioner then gave an unknown amount of dichloroacetate and artesunate 2.5 mg/kg bodyweight intravenously 148 days after surgery.

Cognitive condition declined during the following days with adynamia, severe headaches and signs of delusions. After hospital admission EEG showed no epileptic activity and CT no relevant changes, while blood examinations showed signs of exsiccosis, pancytopenia and markedly increased hepatic enzyme activities. Laboratory parameters stabilized upon fluid substitution.

Two days after hospitalization the patient deteriorated with hypotension, systemic signs of infection and a series of seizures. The family did not wish intensified intervention or mechanical ventilation according to the patient provision, and he died 157 days after surgery. No autopsy was performed. The authors scored RUCAM causality at 6.

article_limitations: Figure 1 plotted values are not printed as numbers and are not estimated; blood count and enzyme values appear only as qualitative trends in the visual submission, not as facts.
No serial per-patient numeric table exists in the article text; Table 1 is a single RUCAM scoring table and Table 2 is a literature survey of animal studies.
Cause of death is speculative and no autopsy was performed; causation of toxicity by DCA and ART is hedged by the authors.
The dose of DCA, its route and the exact day of hospital admission are not stated.
Abstract says death 10 days after the infusion while the timeline gives 9 days (148 to 157 days after surgery).
